issues.description: Constructor parameter order for Meal is inconsistent between the problem statement/solution and the template. The problem UML and the solution implement Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template's Meal constructor is declared as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch will confuse students about the correct constructor signature and will cause compilation or usage errors when following the provided Main examples or the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor signature to match the UML and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients). Keep parameter order consistent across template files and examples so students can instantiate Meal as shown in the Main example.

issues.description: Within the template repository there is an internal contradiction: Main uses the Meal constructor as new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...}) but the template Meal class defines the constructor with reversed parameters (String[] ingredients, String name). This internal mismatch will cause compile-time errors in the example code and confuse students about which signature to implement or use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template files: either update Main to call the constructor with the template's parameter order, or (preferably) update the template Meal constructor to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) so the example in Main matches the Meal API and the problem specification.

issues.description: Constructor parameter ordering for Meal is inconsistent: the problem statement (and solution) specify Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) but the template Meal class defines the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch (also visible in the template Main usage which assumes the name-first signature) creates confusion and can lead to compilation or usage errors when students follow the examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (reordering the parameters) and update any usages in the template (e.g., Main) to pass name first, aligning template with the problem statement and solution.
